text: Bicep's equivalent of a Terraform variable block is the param keyword — supplied at deployment time, never hardcoded. A globally-unique name like a storage account name gets no default; there isn't a sensible one to give it.

A decorator restricts what a parameter accepts, catching a bad value before deployment. Allowed limits a SKU to what Azure actually supports; minLength and maxLength match Azure Storage's real naming rule.
A var never comes from outside the file — a computed value derived from a parameter, used to avoid repeating the same expression.
VS Code's Bicep extension type-checks a file live. A value that violates a decorator gets flagged in the Problems pane before you ever run a deployment command.
Params for the outside, vars for the inside, a live type-checker in between. Next up: deploying a resource group.
